content: 1. Quinine increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Quinine and ponesimod both increase each other's effects by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If treatment is considered, consult a cardiologist. Generally, these drugs should not be initiated in patients concurrently taking QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties, such as heart rate-lowering calcium channel blockers (e.g., verapamil, diltiazem). 3. Both primaquine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Quinine increases the effects of protamine through an unknown mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Quinine enhances the effects of rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Quinine increases the level or effect of repotrectinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, repotrectinib decreases the level or effect of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Repotrectinib is a CYP3A4 inducer, and coadministration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes can reduce efficacy is not recommended unless otherwise specified in the prescribing information. 7. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Quinine increases the level or effect of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 9. Quinine increases the level or effect of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If used, monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if necessary. 10. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Quinine enhances the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Both sevoflurane and quinine increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Quinine increases the level or effect of siponimod by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of siponimod with drugs causing moderate CYP2C9 and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibition is not recommended. 14. Both siponimod and quinine increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Sotorasib decreases the level or effect of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the CYP3A4 substrate for dosage modifications. 16. Sotorasib decreases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage modifications. 17. Quinine enhances the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Tepotinib increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its approved product labeling. 19. Both tetrabenazine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Tipranavir increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Quinine increases the level or effect of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Product labeling for oral topotecan recommends avoiding concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors; the interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 22. Quinine increases the level or effect of tucatinib by an unspecified mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 23. Quinine increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 24. Both quinine and vandetanib increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with drugs known to prolong the QT interval; if such a drug must be used, more frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 25. Quinine enhances the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Both vemurafenib and quinine increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with drugs that prolong the QT interval is not recommended. 27. Quinine increases the level or effect of venetoclax by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. Monitor more closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 28. Quinine increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 29. Quinine increases the levels of vortioxetine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Decrease the vortioxetine dose by 50% when coadministered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 30. Both albuterol and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Quinine increases the level or effect of amantadine by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of quinine or quinidine with amantadine has been shown to reduce the renal clearance of amantadine by approximately 30%. 32. Amiodarone increases the level or effect of quinine by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Both amiodarone and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Both amitriptyline and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Both amoxapine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Both anagrelide and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Both apomorphine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Both arformoterol and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Both arsenic trioxide and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Both artemether/lumefantrine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Both asenapine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Quinine increases the level or effect of atogepant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Quinine increases the level or effect of avapritinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Quinine increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Both azithromycin and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Both quinine and bedaquiline increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 46. Quinine increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor or titrate the substrate dose when berotralstat is coadministered with narrow therapeutic index drugs that are CYP3A substrates. 47. Quinine increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg PO once, then 40 mg PO daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 48. Blinatumomab increases the levels of quinine by decreasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Treatment initiation causes transient cytokine release that may suppress CYP450 enzymes; the highest drug-drug interaction risk is during the first 9 days of the first cycle and the first 2 days of the second cycle in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index. 49. Both bosutinib and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Quinine increases the level or effect of brexpiprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 51. Brodalumab may normalize the formation of CYP450 enzymes by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. Upon initiation or discontinuation of brodalumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, consider monitoring for therapeutic effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Both quinine and bupivacaine implant increase each other's toxicity by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Local anesthetics may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when concurrently exposed to drugs that also cause methemoglobinemia. 53. Both capecitabine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Carbamazepine decreases the level or effect of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Cenobamate decreases the level or effect of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 56. Quinine increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Both chlorpromazine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Cimetidine increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Both ciprofloxacin and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin elicits minimal effects on the QT interval. Exercise caution if used in combination with other drugs known to affect the QT interval or in patients with other risk factors. 60. Both quinine and citalopram increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with caution when using drugs that may prolong the QT interval. 61. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Both clomipramine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Both clozapine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Crizotinib increases the levels of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be needed for coadministered drugs that are predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. Both crizotinib and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Crofelemer increases the levels of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. 67. Cyclosporine increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Quinine increases the level or effect of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl < 30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl < 50 mL/min. 69. Dabrafenib decreases the level or effect of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 70. Danicopan increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates; consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 71. Both dasatinib and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Deferasirox decreases the level or effect of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Both degarelix and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Both desipramine and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 75. Both quinine and deutetrabenazine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances may increase the risk of torsade de pointes and/or sudden death in association with drugs that prolong the QTc interval (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, coadministration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, presence of congenital QT prolongation). 76. Digoxin increases the level or effect of quinine by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Diltiazem increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Both disopyramide and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Dofetilide increases the level or effect of quinine by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Both dofetilide and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Both dolasetron and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Both droperidol and quinine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Dulaglutide slows gastric emptying and may impact the absorption of concomitantly administered oral medications. Be particularly cautious when coadministered with drugs that have a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Dupilumab may alter the formation of CYP450 enzymes by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. Upon initiation or discontinuation of dupilumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, consider monitoring for therapeutic effect. Use caution and monitor closely.
